title: Trades: which piece goes, which stays
outcomes: Compares the pieces you give up and keep before trading
Chooses the trade that removes the enemy's most active piece

steps.text:
A trade changes two things: **the piece you give up** and **the piece you keep.** Before trading, ask what the enemy piece is doing for him (holding an outpost, attacking, defending) and what your recapture will look like.
Trading just because you can does neither job.

steps.caption: Black to move. Which trade is best?

line.say: The bishop takes the knight on c5.

steps.text: When two trades are possible, compare them. **Rule of thumb:** give up the piece that matters less, keep the one that fits your pawns and plans, and prefer the trade that removes his most active piece. Always look at the recapture before you take.

steps.title: Same target, a different piece takes
steps.prompt: Black could also take the knight with the bishop. Is 1...Bxd5 as good as 1...Nxd5? Predict first, then check.
Before you compared the trades: which of your pieces did you want to keep, and why?
